question: Please provide a list of the top three revenue-generating films for each actor, along with the average revenue per actor in those films, calculated by dividing the total film revenue equally among the actors for each film.
sql:
WITH film_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        i.film_id,
        SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue
    FROM payment p
    JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
    JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    GROUP BY i.film_id
),
film_actor_count AS (
    SELECT 
        film_id,
        COUNT(actor_id) AS num_actors
    FROM film_actor
    GROUP BY film_id
),
actor_film_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        fa.actor_id,
        a.first_name,
        a.last_name,
        f.film_id,
        f.title,
        fr.total_revenue,
        ROUND(fr.total_revenue * 1.0 / fac.num_actors, 2) AS per_actor_share
    FROM film_actor fa
    JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
    JOIN film f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
    JOIN film_revenue fr ON fa.film_id = fr.film_id
    JOIN film_actor_count fac ON fa.film_id = fac.film_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        film_id,
        title,
        total_revenue,
        per_actor_share,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id ORDER BY per_actor_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM actor_film_revenue
)
SELECT 
    r.actor_id,
    r.first_name,
    r.last_name,
    r.film_id,
    r.title,
    r.total_revenue,
    r.per_actor_share,
    ROUND(AVG(r.per_actor_share) OVER (PARTITION BY r.actor_id), 2) AS avg_revenue_per_actor
FROM ranked r
WHERE r.rk <= 3
ORDER BY r.actor_id, r.rk

How this database is organised (written by an LLM from the tables' notes and keys):
Transaction tables are payment, rental, and inventory, recording financial activity, film loans, and physical stock. Lookup tables include actor, address, category, city, country, customer, film, language, staff, and store, describing entities and their attributes. The film_actor and film_category tables act as junctions linking films to actors and categories. Connections flow as follows: customer links to address and store; staff links to address and store; store links to address and staff. City links to country. Film links to language. Inventory links to film and store. Rental links to customer, inventory, and staff. Payment links to customer, staff, and rental.

    JOIN film f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
    JOIN film_revenue fr ON fa.film_id = fr.film_id
    JOIN film_actor_count fac ON fa.film_id = fac.film_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        film_id,
        title,
        total_revenue,
        per_actor_share,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id ORDER BY per_actor_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM actor_film_revenue
)
SELECT 
    r.actor_id,
    r.first_name,
    r.last_name,
    r.film_id,
    r.title,
    r.total_revenue,
    r.per_actor_share,
    ROUND(AVG(r.per_actor_share) OVER (PARTITION BY r.actor_id), 2) AS avg_revenue_per_actor
FROM ranked r
WHERE r.rk <= 3
ORDER BY r.actor_id, r.rk
